name: American Made Apparel Manufacturing., Inc.
old_description: If you’re looking for full-service, cut and sew company professionals, talk to American Made Apparel Manufacturing in Denver. We have over 30 years of experience helping our clients develop high-quality, custom apparel (and so much more) from our fully-equipped facility. Using the latest equipment and methods, we can mass-produce just about anything you can imagine.
about:
American Made Apparel Manufacturing, Inc. was founded in 1996 in Aurora, Colorado. The company operates a fully equipped facility in the Denver metropolitan area, specializing in domestic apparel production.

The shop provides end-to-end cut-and-sew services, from design consultation and pattern drafting using CAD/CAM software to size grading via Accumark Gerber technology, prototype development, fabric laying and cutting on over 24 yards of table space, machine-assisted cutting, sewing, and final inspection. Every order is tagged, packed by size, and shipped or held for pickup.

Clients include sports-apparel brands and businesses seeking custom garment manufacturing; the company cites a collaboration with Fire Within as an example of its custom product process. It serves brands, designers, and companies needing domestic production runs of varying sizes.

American Made emphasizes its "100% Made in America" designation, stringent quality standards, and open communication throughout each project. The company states that it differentiates itself by guiding clients through every step—from initial sketches to finished goods—and by treating each client as its only client.

name: Amphenol Custom Cable
old_description: Amphenol Custom Cable specializes in network infrastructure, modernization, and wireless solutions to help you build and maintain a strong network foundation. We meet the demand for greater, faster bandwidth with engineering expertise, speed, scalability, and security in mind at the outset.
about:
Amphenol Custom Cable is headquartered in Tampa, Florida, where it has operated for over 35 years as a supply chain partner. The company is a division of Amphenol, a global leader in interconnect solutions with operations across six continents. Founded as a custom cable assembly specialist, it has grown into an integrated resource combining engineering, procurement, manufacturing, and deployment teams.

The company operates a 38,000-square-foot production facility in Tampa running multiple assembly shifts and production lines, supported by a global supply chain. Its Assembly Division produces fiber optic, RF, and copper cable assemblies — from discrete wire harnesses to complex box builds — with capabilities including automated cutting, stripping, crimping, overmolding, and potting. The Network Services Division provides installation, testing, and commissioning of data and communications infrastructure from operating centers in Tampa, Orlando, Dallas, Charlotte, and Atlanta. All assemblies are built domestically, 100% inspected, and shipped with no minimum order quantity.

Customers span telecommunications and broadband providers, hyperscale data centers, military and aerospace programs, industrial robotics and automation firms, and medical high-reliability applications. The company cites telecommunications companies, service providers, online retailers, supermarket chains, hospitals, and sports facilities as typical clients for its network installation services.

Amphenol Custom Cable emphasizes speed and flexibility: its online PunchOut configurator lets engineers design custom assemblies and place orders directly from procurement systems, with assemblies shipping within days. The company holds ISO 9001:2015, TL9000, IPC/WHMA-A-620, and ITAR registrations, and positions its integrated global Amphenol backbone as a differentiator for rapid scaling and supply chain resilience.

name: Amtech
old_description: “We have had a long working relationship with Amtech since 1998. The company prides itself in coming through for the customer at critical times and never giving up on tough projects - they deliver on that message and go beyond normal customer service duties. They produce high quality assembly services, are easy to reach and always respond to customer needs. Amtech is our first go-to place for PCB assembly services.”
about:
Amtech is a family-owned contract electronics manufacturer based in Troy, Michigan, founded in 1998. The company operates from a facility and has served OEMs, hardware startups, and venture-backed companies for more than three decades as a build-to-print partner, meaning customers retain design ownership while Amtech manufactures to exact specifications.

The company provides end-to-end electronics manufacturing services including PCB assembly (turnkey SMT and through-hole from prototype to mid-volume production), box build and mechanical assembly, custom wire harnesses with 100% electrical testing, functional and in-circuit testing, and product development support such as DFM/DFA. Production runs on AmtechOS, a proprietary ERP system, and the business operates on the Entrepreneurial Operating System (EOS). The firm emphasizes high-mix, low-volume programs alongside high-volume production, supported by advanced automation and in-house robotics platforms.

Amtech serves automotive (aftermarket, OEM Tier 2 ceramic substrate programs), industrial automation (20+ year partnerships), IoT, health and safety (mission-critical scale-ups), and defense/UAS supply chains with NDAA-compliant manufacturing. Customer testimonials cite long-term relationships dating to 1998 across automotive, industrial automation, and IoT sectors, with case studies highlighting 8-week program launches, custom PCB design with fixturing, and decade-long ceramic substrate soldering partnerships.

The company positions itself as a technology partner rather than a pure contract manufacturer, offering engagement models from tech facilitator to ODM-style support to production partner, all within a single framework that allows customers to expand services without changing partners, processes, or systems. Its 3R Promise — Reliable, Robust, and Responsive — underpins proactive communication and domestic manufacturing backed by a global supply chain.

name: Andersen Wrecking Co., Inc.
old_description: Andersen Wrecking is one of the leading recyclers in the Midwest. We are family owned and have been serving central Nebraska since 1937 offering dependable, recycled auto and truck parts. We also purchase and recycle ferrous and non-ferrous metal salvage.
about:
Andersen Wrecking Co., Inc. has operated from Kearney, Nebraska since 1937. Founded as a family-owned auto wrecking and recycling yard, the business has grown into one of the Midwest’s recyclers serving central Nebraska and beyond. Since its founding, the company has provided the region with high-quality new, aftermarket, and recycled auto parts.

The company maintains an extensive inventory searchable nationwide through the Car-Part Interchange system, offering components ranging from wiring harnesses and differential assemblies to diesel particulate filters and bumper assemblies. It also purchases and recycles ferrous and non-ferrous metal salvage, providing dismantling and metal recycling services.

Customers include automotive repair shops, collision centers, individual vehicle owners, and scrap metal buyers across the Midwest. The business serves both retail and wholesale customers, with warranty options available. The company’s automotive professionals assist with locating specific parts, whether for foreign or domestic vehicles.

Andersen Wrecking emphasizes its long-standing presence as a recycler, combining a large parts inventory with nationwide search capability and a commitment to dependable recycled components.

name: Anfinsen Plastic Molding Inc.
old_description: Anfinsen Plastic Molding was founded in 1935 and started with molding small size molded parts that were a result of technical limitations of that era. We have since advanced in to molding large scale parts with complex geometries and materials, as well as a full assembly warehouse to manage customer supplied materials, like hardware, metal, custom-packaging, and other polymer based goods to complete your finished product. With a full inventory barcoding system, we are capable of managing large-scale programs that need storage till fulfillment and then on to the next project.
about:
Anfinsen Plastic Molding operates from Oswego, Illinois, where it was founded in 1935. The company began by molding small parts constrained by the technical limitations of the era and has since expanded into large-scale, complex-geometry molding alongside a full assembly warehouse that manages customer-supplied hardware, metal, custom packaging, and other polymer goods. Ownership structure and founders are not disclosed in public materials.

The shop runs 31 injection molding presses ranging from 40 to 1,000 tons, producing millions of thermoplastic parts annually from materials such as ABS, polycarbonate, HIPS, acetal, and acrylic. A 100,000-square-foot assembly facility provides discrete assembly, riveting, sonic welding, heat bending, and barcode-driven inventory management for customer-supplied components. In-house decorating capabilities include painting, custom masking, pad printing, hot stamping, and color matching. Tooling engineering, quality control, and logistics fulfillment with ERP-backed warehousing and drop shipping round out the service offering.

Anfinsen has maintained a decades-long presence in the point-of-purchase display industry, serving retail channels that include Walmart, Walgreens, Target, gas stations, and convenience stores. The company works closely with the marketing and design firms behind those brands and cites customers such as Edge Products, Kirkland Foods, and Global Brands. Projects typically involve time-sensitive retail rollouts where speed and on-the-fly problem solving are critical.

Leadership emphasizes a culture of urgency developed in fast-paced, competitive markets. The company states it quotes custom projects quickly, provides a detailed roadmap, and excels when pressure is highest, aiming to deliver without sacrificing quality.

name: Antaya Technologies Corporation
old_description: Antaya Technologies Corp. is the global leading manufacturer of on-glass connectors for the automotive industry worldwide. Additionally, we supply custom connection solutions for the solar panel industry, electronic module manufacturers, and architectural glass applications.
about:
Antaya Technologies Corporation is headquartered in Warwick, Rhode Island. The company began with initial work providing terminals and controlled soldering equipment for heated automotive glass, later expanding into a global supplier of on-glass power and signal connection systems and automated soldering equipment.

Antaya manufactures on-glass connectors and custom connection solutions for automotive, solar, electronic module, and architectural glass applications. Its vertically integrated facilities handle solder casting, reflow, rolling, slitting, stamping, welding, injection molding, fluxing, assembly, and tooling across six global locations, allowing strict quality control and rapid response to customer needs.

The company serves the automotive glass and electronics sectors, solar energy producers, electro-chromatic glass makers, electronic module manufacturers, and industrial component suppliers. Its products are used in heated automotive glass, solar panels, and architectural glass installations.

Antaya emphasizes its pioneer status in glass soldering technology and its vertical integration as key differentiators, enabling custom alloy casting to customer specifications, lead-free and leaded solder alloys meeting automotive standards, and a reflow process that delivers exceptional uniformity and material yield for complex designs.

name: Approved Sheet Metal
old_description: Founded by accomplished sheet metal fabrication industry experts. Approved Sheet metal (ASM) is an American sheet metal fabricator of custom precision prototype and low volume production sheet metal fabricated parts.
about:
Approved Sheet Metal operates from Hudson, New Hampshire. The company was formed in 2020 by experienced sheet metal fabrication leaders who wanted to support American manufacturing by improving how parts are designed, made, and delivered. The business is privately owned; no specific ownership designations such as veteran- or woman-owned are publicly claimed.

The shop specializes in custom precision prototype and low-volume production sheet metal fabrication. Core processes include laser cutting, forming, welding, hardware insertion, powder coating, silk screening, and a range of finishing options from mill finish to Class A cosmetic. The facility handles quantities from a single piece up to 5,000 parts, turning thousands of unique part numbers each month. In-house capabilities span cutting, forming, welding, finishing, and assembly.

Customers are primarily product developers and buyers across a range of industries who need fast, precise sheet metal parts. The company emphasizes support for American manufacturing and works with clients nationwide on projects such as enclosures, weldments, brackets, RF/EMI shields, chassis, cabinets, and 19-inch rack components.

The founders built the company on speed and technology: quotes are returned within hours, flat laser-cut parts can ship the same day if ordered by 10 a.m. EST, and formed prototypes typically deliver in two to five days. The operation is ISO 9001:2015 certified and ITAR registered, and runs on a custom ERP with real-time material inventory to keep lead times short.

name: Architectural System Fabricators
old_description: Yes. Custom fabrication is at the core of what we do. We work closely with architects, contractors, and construction firms to fabricate metal components to exact specifications. Whether you provide your own drawings or need design support, our team is equipped to deliver precision-crafted solutions.
about:
Architectural System Fabricators LLC operates from a facility on Industrial Drive in Southington, Connecticut. The company was founded in 2019 by Adam, who grew up in construction working alongside his father before expanding into commercial metalwork and investing in advanced machinery for his own projects. Recognizing a gap in the market for reliable, high-quality architectural metal fabrication, he established ASF to focus on precision, speed, and customer collaboration.

The shop specializes exclusively in architectural metalwork — not general steel fabrication — producing custom ACM panels, brake-formed components, CNC-routed designs, and long-folded profiles up to 20 feet. Core processes include brake forming, CNC routing, laser cutting, punching, in-house coil processing, welding, folding, shearing, and both liquid and powder coating. Equipment highlights include Connecticut's only long-folding machine, advanced CNC routers, and high-precision laser cutters. The team brings over 55 years of combined architectural metal fabrication experience.

ASF serves architects, contractors, and construction firms on commercial, institutional, and industrial projects across the United States, with a regional focus on Fairfield County, southern Connecticut, and New England. Past work includes ACM panels and brake-formed trim for the Greenwich Residence, aluminum soffit panels for the Plainville School, and 100,000 square feet of custom louver blades for a single project. The company also fabricated components for the CJ Huang Recreation Center and has worked with Laminators Inc.

The company differentiates itself through its architectural-only focus, in-house coil processing, and the long-folding capability unique in Connecticut. It emphasizes design support, turning concepts into fabrication-ready drawings, and nationwide shipping with secure crating from single pallets to full truckloads.
